# ECON 0100 | Vignette C2 | Taxes + Subsidies

::: solution

# Solutions

:::

*Answers and work are shown in the red blocks.*

Before the connection between Glittering Gum and Starlight Sneeze was established, the fiscal arm of the Ministry implemented a 3 Coin subsidy on every sale of Glittering Gum, to put a little sparkle into Hogsmeade’s conversations. The Demand and Supply curves are the same as in Vignette C1.

With no known externalities, use a graph to illustrate the impact of the subsidy on the market.

::::

::::: solution

Buyer’s Price $P_b$: $12$ coins. Seller’s Price $P_s$: $15$ coins. Subsidy Quantity $Q^{Sub}$: $36$ pieces of gum. Dead Weight Loss: $6$ coins.

:::: {.columns gutter=1em}

::: column

From Vignette C1, demand is $P = 30 - \tfrac{1}{2} Q$ and supply is $P = 6 + \tfrac{1}{4} Q$. Without the subsidy, buyers and sellers face one price:

$$
30 - \tfrac{1}{2} Q = 6 + \tfrac{1}{4} Q \quad\Rightarrow\quad Q = 32, \quad P = 14
$$

A subsidy is the tax wedge turned around: the seller now receives $3$ more than the buyer pays, so the wedge sits to the *right* of the no-policy equilibrium:

$$
P_s = 3 + P_b \quad\Rightarrow\quad 6 + \tfrac{1}{4} Q = 3 + (30 - \tfrac{1}{2} Q) \quad\Rightarrow\quad Q = 36
$$

so $P_b = 30 - 18 = 12$ and $P_s = 6 + 9 = 15$.

:::

::: column

![Subsidy equilibrium](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){width=100%}

:::

::::

Past $32$, supply (marginal cost) is above demand (marginal benefit): the $33$rd through $36$th pieces cost $14.25$ to $15$ coins to make, but buyers value them at $14$ down to $12$. They trade only because the Ministry pays the difference. The triangle between the curves over those $4$ pieces is the deadweight loss:

$$
\text{DWL} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times (36 - 32) = 6
$$

For reference, since the graph shows them: buyers pay $14 - 12 = 2$ less than before and sellers receive $15 - 14 = 1$ more, so buyers get more of the subsidy (demand is steeper). Consumer surplus rises from $\frac{1}{2} \times 32 \times 16 = 256$ to $\frac{1}{2} \times 36 \times 18 = 324$ and producer surplus from $\frac{1}{2} \times 32 \times 8 = 128$ to $\frac{1}{2} \times 36 \times 9 = 162$, but the Ministry pays $3 \times 36 = 108$. Check: the gains, $68 + 34 = 102$, are the spending less the deadweight loss, $108 - 6$.

With no externality, the market’s $32$ was already efficient, so the subsidy buys $4$ pieces too many. Once the Starlight Sneeze is counted (Vignette C1), the efficient quantity is $24$, so the Ministry was paying to push the market the wrong way; Vignette C3 takes that up.

:::::
